records.student_text: Kai walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Kai walks at 2 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Kai can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.
records.student_html:
Kai walks toward the front of a train moving east at 9 m/s. Kai walks at 2 m/s relative to the train. Explain how Kai can be moving relative to the ground while also being described using a different motion relative to the train.

  1. Kai must have the same velocity in every reference frame.
  2. Kai is at rest relative to the ground because the train is the only valid frame.
  3. Reference frames change the object’s mass, which changes its motion.
  4. Relative to the train, Kai moves east at 2 m/s; relative to the ground, Kai moves east at 11 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
choices: Kai must have the same velocity in every reference frame.
Kai is at rest relative to the ground because the train is the only valid frame.
Reference frames change the object’s mass, which changes its motion.
Relative to the train, Kai moves east at 2 m/s; relative to the ground, Kai moves east at 11 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
records.answer: Relative to the train, Kai moves east at 2 m/s; relative to the ground, Kai moves east at 11 m/s. Motion depends on the chosen reference frame.
records.solution_text: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.
records.solution_html: Use one reference frame at a time. The train-frame motion is the walking speed; the ground-frame motion combines the train motion and walking motion because both are east.

records.evidence_job: Use the target relationship with physically meaningful data, units, and interpretation to determine the requested motion quantity.
records.student_action: Identify the relevant values, apply the appropriate relationship, report units, and interpret the result in context.
records.intended_reasoning: Use the target relationship with physically meaningful data, units, and interpretation to determine the requested motion quantity.
records.student_text: For ideal free fall from rest, use d = ½gt² with g ≈ 10 m/s². Compare the total distance fallen after 2 s and 3 s. Then explain why a coffee filter falling at terminal speed would not follow this same pattern.
records.student_html: For ideal free fall from rest, use d = ½gt² with g ≈ 10 m/s². Compare the total distance fallen after 2 s and 3 s. Then explain why a coffee filter falling at terminal speed would not follow this same pattern.
records.answer: After 2 s: 20 m; after 3 s: 45 m. The ideal distance grows with t². A filter with significant air resistance is not in ideal free fall and can reach nearly constant speed.
records.solution_text: d=5t² gives 20 m and 45 m. Significant air resistance changes the acceleration, so the ideal free-fall model no longer applies.
records.solution_html: d=5t² gives 20 m and 45 m. Significant air resistance changes the acceleration, so the ideal free-fall model no longer applies.

records.primary_i_can: I can connect motion diagrams, data tables, and graphs to written descriptions of motion and critique an incorrect motion model and revise it using evidence.
records.evidence_job: Interpret, construct, compare, or critique a motion representation while preserving the physical quantities and relationships in the target.
records.student_action: Use the supplied data/representation or construct the requested representation, then explain the motion evidence it shows.
records.intended_reasoning: Interpret, construct, compare, or critique a motion representation while preserving the physical quantities and relationships in the target.
records.student_text: A position–time graph is shown. Write a motion description consistent with the graph, then identify one common incorrect interpretation and correct it.
records.student_html: A position–time graph is shown. Write a motion description consistent with the graph, then identify one common incorrect interpretation and correct it.
records.answer: The object moves in the positive direction at constant velocity 1 m/s. The graph height represents position, not physical height above the ground.
records.solution_text: The straight-line position–time graph has constant slope 1 m/s, so velocity is constant. The vertical axis is position, so it should not be read as a picture of a hill.
records.solution_html: The straight-line position–time graph has constant slope 1 m/s, so velocity is constant. The vertical axis is position, so it should not be read as a picture of a hill.
